data.narrative:
Fuse Energy is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by JC Btaiche, currently valued at $200M+ post-money on $78M raised to date. The nuclear energy sector comp universe includes 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms, with notable peers including Oklo, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable triangulation approach given insufficient narrow-peer density in the nuclear sector. Using the last post-money valuation of $200M as the base and applying a standard 2.0x multiplier for Series A to next-stage progression yields $400M. Peer-median analysis was not viable; while 3 same-sector comps exist, none met the threshold of 3+ datapoints within same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filters, making sector-wide medians unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $340M to $460M, with a median estimate of $400M. This range reflects the stage-progression methodology anchored to last round post-money, with the bounds derived from sensitivity to execution risk and capital requirements typical of early-stage frontier energy ventures. Key uncertainties include technology validation milestones, regulatory pathway clarity, and construction/deployment timelines—factors that will materially inform next financing round pricing. A more robust peer-driven valuation would require either: (1) achieving sufficient density of same-stage nuclear comps, or (2) comparative analysis to adjacent advanced energy sectors if justified by business model homology.
